Alex — thanks for sending this over and for the list. We’ve reviewed the PDF and can provide a focused package that maps directly to each question. High level answers:

- SAML/OIDC: Both supported. We support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML SSO across our Hosted and Dedicated deployments; OIDC (authorization_code + PKCE) is supported for web/native integrations. IdP compatibility: Okta, Azure AD, PingFederate, OneLogin, and most SAML 2.0 IdPs we’ve tested.
- SCIM v2 provisioning: We support SCIM 2.0 core with user and group provisioning, incremental syncs, and a recommended bookkeeping strategy for conflict resolution (last-writer-wins with optional source_of_truth tag).
- RBAC & delegated admin: Product includes tenant-scoped roles and a delegated admin model. We provide several built-in roles (Org Admin, Security Admin, Support Engineer, Read-only Auditor) and allow creation of custom roles with fine-grained permissions.
- Audit logs: Audit events for admin actions, provisioning changes, and authentication events are stored and can be exported in JSON/CSV; retention configurable per contract (default 90 days for hosted tier, longer for Dedicated/Private).

What I’m attaching is our compiled capability matrix and a proposed admin-delegation runbook draft. Connor has added a short technical appendix for SCIM attribute mapping and health-check endpoints. Kimberly — tagging you for compliance / retention confirmation.

Next steps:
- We can turn the attached matrix into a completed RFI response within 48 hours.
- Recommend a 30-minute technical sync Wed (Aug 25) 11am PT to walk through SCIM mapping and delegated admin flows.

Would you like us to return the answers inline in the PDF, or provide an annotated spreadsheet?

Best,

Alex / team — adding a few technical clarifications based on the specific items in the PDF to make the SCIM and SSO items actionable for your engineers:

SCIM provisioning notes:
- Supported endpoints: /Users, /Groups, /ServiceProviderConfig. We implement /Bulk for bulk provisioning (per RFC 7644 bulk extension) with rate limits configurable per tenant.
- Attribute mapping: Primary identifiers are "id" (SCIM id) and externalId (IdP-provided). We recommend externalId as the authoritative mapping for IdP-driven updates. Attached is a sample mapping CSV for common IdP attributes (email, name, department, manager) to our internal attributes.
- Conflict resolution: By default last-writer-wins. For Dedicated/Private customers we can enable a source_of_truth marker and enforce server-side checks to block conflicting updates.
- Connectivity: We provide a health-check endpoint (/scim/health) and diagnostics logs (last sync status, error counters) in the Console UI and as an API.

SSO and session management:
- SAML bindings: HTTP-Redirect (AuthnRequest) and HTTP-POST supported. We support signed AuthnRequests and encrypted assertions when required.
- OIDC: Authorization code flow with PKCE; token introspection endpoint available for long-running sessions. Session length configurable; token refresh handled by standard refresh_token flow (rotating refresh tokens supported).

Audit & evidence:
- Admin actions are logged with user, role, action, target resource, timestamp, and request_id. Exportable via API as newline-delimited JSON. Default retention 90d; can be extended.

Attachments: scim_schema_map.csv (csv, 7KB); sso-test-plan.md (md, 3KB).

I can walk through the mapping in the Wed call and run a live SCIM push to a test tenant if you want.

—Connor
